summary: A controller that refuses the identification function is still a controller, so the refusal has to be recorded as an observation rather than dropped as a failure.

device.description: OpenPLC v3, the soft PLC used by GRFICS and by a great many teaching and test benches
device.derivation: processModbusMessage in modbus.cpp dispatches on the function code through a chain of comparisons. Read Device Identification, function 43 with MEI type 14, is not among them: the closest thing in the file is 0x43, which is 67 decimal and is OpenPLC's own debug read, a different function entirely. So the request falls through to the final branch and is answered by ModbusError with ERR_ILLEGAL_FUNCTION. ModbusError edits the request buffer in place, fixing the length field at three, setting the high bit of the function code and appending the error code.

expect.error_detail: modbus device returned error 1: illegal function
notes: device answered Modbus function 43 with exception 1 (illegal function), so it speaks Modbus but does not support device identification
